newsitem.title: USA: Stocks gain ahead of Fed chairman's testimony.
newsitem.headline: Stocks gain ahead of Fed chairman's testimony.

text.p: Stocks were higher Tuesday, as Wall Street awaited Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony on the economy with an optimism tinged just slightly with caution.
At 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT), the 30-stock Dow was up 16.49 points at 7,923.21 after gaining more than 50 points in early morning.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 16-9 on volume of 302 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 9.22 points to 1,545.45.
The rally was also fuelled by solid earnings reports and bargain-hunting.
"The market seems to believe Greenspan will not say anything extreme," said Barbara Marcin, vice president of Citibank Global Asset Management.
The Fed chief will give the mandatory, semi-annual testimony on the economy and monetary policy to Congress at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT). He will also addess Congress on Wednesday.

Traders will pay attention for anything he said about inflation or stock valuations, analysts said. But some said there was little that Greenspan could say to derail the rosy scenerio for the economy.

"The economy is still performing extremely well. ... The inflation outlook is benign, and it is hard to conceive of a change in interest rates to the upside," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp.
Stocks were also higher because they had been weak recently as investors took some profits, analysts said.

"Investors are using any excuse to be buyers," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "A modest recovery in bonds and, essentially, a three-day decline in stocks, is enough to bring in buyers."
Solid second-quarter earnings results helped push the broader stock market higher, too, analysts said.

Dow component Philip Morris Cos. posted second-quarter earnings of 76 cents a share vs. 66 cents a share in last year's second quarter and in line with the First Call consensus earnings estimate. The company's stock was up 1-12/16 to 42-5/16.
Walt Disney Co. rose 1-10/16 to 76-13/16, after reporting upbeat earnings.
But International Business Machines, whose stock had been strong ahead of its quarterly earnings release late Monday, fell 1-14/16 to 101-13/16.
